identity.description:
Read every page of the deploy poll and wait for every deploy run

## Summary

The deploy watch missed the deploy of a merge on a busy default branch. It read only the first 100 runs of the merge commit, and scheduled workflows put about 1,000 runs on one commit in an hour, so the deploy run was not on that page. It also judged only the newest deploy run, but a monorepo merge starts one deploy workflow per service. Now the watch reads every page, reads only the runs that the merge itself started (push and chained workflow_run events), and prints `deployed` only when every deploy run of the merge finished and at least one succeeded. A failed deploy run prints `deploy-failed` at once. A named `Deploy: workflow:` reads that workflow's own runs on every page.

Closes #146

**Ticket:** [jerridan/crew#146](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/146)
**Type:** Bug fix

---

## Agent context

### Authority

`skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md`, "The deploy poll", owns the rule and states it whole. `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`, "Standing instructions", owns the `Deploy` lines. `docs/design.md` §15.127 (the deploy watch) and the new finding 170.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/delivered-window/scripts/pr-watch.sh`: `wf_check()` is gone. `runs_read()` reads every page. `wf_default()` reads `event=push` and `event=workflow_run` and judges the set of deploy runs. `wf_named()` finds the named workflow's ids through `actions/workflows` and reads `actions/workflows/<id>/runs?head_sha=` on every page, because a repository-wide `head_sha` read returns 1,000 runs at most. A failed runs read makes no `no-deploy` decision; `deploy_timeout()` still runs.
- `skills/delivered-window/scripts/test-pr-watch-deploy.sh`: the stub `gh` serves pages of 100, filters by `head_sha` and `event`, honours `--paginate`, serves the workflow-scoped endpoint and logs each call. New cases for each Outcome of the issue, for failed reads and for the line shape.
- `skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md` and `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`: the prose matches the code.
- `docs/design.md`: finding 170. Both manifests: 0.1.138.

### Constraints that applied

- The line format `<kind> <id> - <time> <text>` and the exit codes did not change; `<id>` stays one token, so `watch-step.py`'s `split(None, 4)` still parses it. The `deployed` text of the default signal now ends `; <n> deploy runs succeeded`.
- Bash with `gh` and `jq` only. A failed read prints no line.
- Not in scope, as the issue says: matching a deploy run by anything other than its name. The deployments rung did not change.

### How this was verified

`bash skills/delivered-window/scripts/test-pr-watch-deploy.sh` (46 of 46), `test-watch-step.sh` (90 of 90) and `test-window-watch.sh` (114 of 114) pass at the head. The test commit 0673c83 fails the first script (31 of 46) on the new cases before the fix. A Codex review read the spec and the plan before any code; its findings (failed reads, the 1,000-run cap of a `head_sha` search, both event streams in one case) are in the code and the tests.

### Known gaps

- No crew run has used the new watch against a real repo.
- A chained deploy that GitHub creates some seconds after its CI run ends can miss the set when another deploy run already succeeded.
- A run that never leaves `queued` or `waiting` on the merge commit holds back `deployed` until the timeout.

# Spec: the deploy watch on a busy default branch (jerridan/crew#146)

Repo: /Users/jerridanquiring/src/crew/.claude/worktrees/issue-146

## The problem

`skills/delivered-window/scripts/pr-watch.sh`'s `wf_check()` reads one page of `actions/runs?head_sha=<merge sha>&per_page=100` and judges the newest run whose name matches. On a default branch with scheduled workflows, a merge commit collects about 1,000 runs in an hour, almost all `schedule` events. The deploy run is not on the first page, so the watch prints nothing. In a monorepo, one merge starts several deploy runs, one per service, and the watch judges only the newest.

## Requirements

R1. **Every page.** The workflow-run rungs of the deploy poll read every page of the runs they query, so a matching run is found at any position in the list.
- AC1: in the seeded test, the merge commit has more than 100 runs over two or more pages, and the deploy run is only on a later page. `deploy-once` prints `deployed`.

R2. **The default rung keeps only the merge's own runs.** With no `environment` and no `workflow` in `run.deploy`, and no GitHub deployments in the repo, the poll counts only runs whose `event` is `push` or `workflow_run`, whose name holds `deploy` or `release` (case-insensitive, as now).
- AC2: in the seeded test, a `schedule` run and a `workflow_dispatch` run named like a deploy, with conclusion `success`, are the only matching names on the merge commit. `deploy-once` prints no `deployed` line.

R3. **The default rung waits for every deploy run of the merge.** The rung judges the set of the matching runs of R2, not the newest one:
- A run whose conclusion is `failure`, `timed_out` or `startup_failure` makes the poll print `deploy-failed` at once. When more than one run failed, the line names the one with the latest `updated_at`, with its id, time and name.
- `deployed` prints only when at least one matching run succeeded, no matching run is still unfinished (its `status` is not `completed`), and no `push` or `workflow_run` run of any name on the merge commit is unfinished. The last condition holds back the ship word while a CI run can still start a chained deploy (a `workflow_run` event).
- A completed run with any other conclusion (`cancelled`, `skipped`, `neutral` and the like) neither blocks nor counts as a success.
- The `deployed` line names the matching run that finished last, and says how many deploy runs succeeded.
- AC3a: two matching runs, one `success` and one `in_progress`: no line.
- AC3b: both `success`: one `deployed` line.
- AC3c: one `success`, one `failure`: one `deploy-failed` line naming the failed run.
- AC3d: one matching run `success`, and a `push` run named `CI` still `in_progress`: no line.

R4. **`Deploy: workflow: <name>` still works for one named workflow.** It reads every page (R1), keeps every event (a named deploy can be a `workflow_dispatch`), and judges the newest run of that name, as now.
- AC4: in the seeded test, `run.deploy.workflow` names a run on a later page: `deployed`. A newer run of that name with `failure`: `deploy-failed`.

R5. **The line format and the exit codes do not change.** Each line is `<kind> <id> - <time> <text>`, with one token for `<id>`. `skills/delivered-window/scripts/watch-step.py` parses it with `split(None, 4)`.
- AC5: `bash skills/delivered-window/scripts/test-watch-step.sh` and `bash skills/delivered-window/scripts/test-window-watch.sh` still pass.

R6. **The references agree with the code.** `skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md`'s "The deploy poll" owns the rule and states R1 to R4. Every other file that states how the poll picks or judges a run says the same or points at that section, among them `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`'s `Deploy` lines and `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md`. The comment above `wf_check()` and the script header say the same.
- AC6: a reviewer reads each of those passages beside the code and finds no disagreement. No passage says "the newest run" of the default rung.

R7. **The test covers each rule.** `skills/delivered-window/scripts/test-pr-watch-deploy.sh`'s stub `gh` answers `--paginate`, the `page` parameter and the `event` query parameter the way GitHub does, so AC1 to AC4 test the real queries. Every case that passed before still passes.
- AC7: `bash skills/delivered-window/scripts/test-pr-watch-deploy.sh` exits 0.

## Global constraints

- `pr-watch.sh` stays bash, with `gh` and `jq` as its only tools.
- A failed `gh` read is no result for that poll, as now: it never prints a line.
- The default rung queries by event: one paginated `actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>&event=push` read and one with `event=workflow_run`. It never reads the unfiltered list of the merge commit's runs, so `schedule` runs cost it no calls.
- ASD-STE100 for every prose change, and `writing-standard.md` for every reference. A rule lives in one file.
- A change under `skills/` bumps `version` in both manifests; the orchestrator owns the value, and the project lead sets it at the PR.
- A new `docs/design.md` §15 finding records the change; the project lead writes it.

## Non-goals

- Recognising a deploy run by anything other than its name (the issue's "Not in scope"). `Deploy` stays the override, and `manual` stays the answer for a deploy inside the CI workflow or outside GitHub.
- The deployments rung (`environment`, or a repo with GitHub deployments) does not change.
- The `no-deploy` rules (the 2-minute and 10-minute waits) do not change, except that they see the runs of R2.
- Many named workflows in `Deploy`.

</details>
